proposals.title: Multi-Scale Neighborhood Composition Analysis
proposals.summary: This analysis targets the dissection of tissue microenvironment heterogeneity by characterizing local neighborhood compositions at multiple spatial scales. It leverages spatial transcriptomics data combined with robust quality control and normalization to accurately map cellular distributions. The core strategy involves constructing spatial neighborhood graphs and applying clustering algorithms to uncover nuanced differences in cell type mixtures, while also testing sensitivity to cell density variations. By explicitly addressing artifacts due to spatial resolution and segmentation, this approach reinforces distinct identification of neighborhood heterogeneity as highlighted by the critics.

proposals.title: Recurrent Microenvironment Discovery Across Tissue Regions
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on identifying and validating recurrent microenvironment patterns across different tissue regions or samples. It uses high-resolution spatial omics data to delineate microdomains via advanced dimensionality reduction and spatial graph construction. Clustering techniques combined with permutation-based differential expression analysis help pinpoint consistent cellular assemblies and molecular signatures. This method addresses critic concerns by integrating comparative analyses across samples, ensuring reproducible detection of biologically meaningful microenvironments.

proposals.title: Differential Neighborhood Analysis Between Conditions
proposals.summary: The goal of this analysis is to uncover spatial neighborhoods that differ across biological conditions or tissue compartments. Using spatial transcriptomics data, the strategy incorporates rigorous normalization and adaptive spatial graph construction to compare neighborhood compositions. Differential testing and cluster validation are employed to highlight regions where cell-type distributions significantly deviate between conditions. This approach emphasizes condition-level comparisons and statistical rigor, directly addressing critiques about detailed neighborhood-level differential analysis.

proposals.title: Spatially Informed Ligand–Receptor Interaction Mapping
proposals.summary: This analysis is designed to integrate ligand–receptor interaction data with spatial context to decipher intercellular communication within tissue microenvironments. By leveraging both molecular expression profiles and precise spatial coordinates, the workflow constructs interaction networks overlaid on spatial neighborhood graphs. Clustering and gene signature scoring strategies are applied to reveal communication-active domains, particularly at disease boundaries. The method meets critic guidance by distinctly focusing on spatially contextual cell–cell interaction patterns alongside classical neighborhood composition analysis.

proposals.title: Resolution and Density Sensitivity in Neighborhood Inference
proposals.summary: This study systematically evaluates the effects of spatial resolution and local cell density on the inference of tissue microenvironments. Utilizing spatial omics data, the approach employs adaptive normalization and sensitivity tests to calibrate neighborhood graph construction. Comparative analyses across varying segmentation scales ensure that the detected neighborhoods reflect true biological patterns instead of technical artifacts. The methodology directly responds to critiques by innovatively addressing the impact of resolution and density on spatial analyses.

proposals.title: Boundary-Centric Analysis of Tissue Microdomains
proposals.summary: Focusing on regions at tissue or disease boundaries, this analysis seeks to delineate microenvironment transitions that are often obscured in bulk analyses. The strategy involves integrating local spatial coordinates with molecular profiles to define neighborhoods that span tissue interfaces. Rigorous spatial graph construction paired with sensitivity-adjusted clustering enables the detection of subtle shifts in composition and function near boundaries. This targeted approach responds to critic recommendations by emphasizing distinct spatial comparisons and inter-condition evaluations at crucial margins.

proposals.title: Inter-Sample Comparative Neighborhood Profiling
proposals.summary: This proposal aims to compare spatial microenvironmental patterns across multiple tissue samples to identify inter-sample variability and conserved features. It utilizes spatial transcriptomics coupled with robust quality controls and normalization to build comparable neighborhood profiles across samples. Advanced clustering and differential expression analysis are then applied to identify common versus unique microdomains. This approach expands on traditional methods by strategically benchmarking neighborhood similarities and differences across samples, satisfying critic calls for inter-patient and inter-sample comparisons.

proposals.title: Integrated Spatial Graph and Differential Expression Microdomain Discovery
proposals.summary: This analysis integrates spatial graph construction with rigorous differential expression testing to identify biologically meaningful microdomains. It utilizes spatial transcriptomics data to meticulously construct multi-scale neighborhood graphs that capture both continuous gradients and discrete clusters. A combination of clustering, permutation controls, and gene signature scoring is applied to validate the identified zones. Emphasizing clear statistical validation and molecular correlation, this method distinguishes itself by combining neighborhood composition with robust differential analyses as per critics' guidance.

proposals.title: Adaptive Normalization and Clustering for Spatial Transcriptomics
proposals.summary: This proposal focuses on optimizing spatial transcriptomics analysis through adaptive normalization, which is critical for accurate neighborhood inference. The approach involves careful quality control, sensitivity analyses, and spatially informed dimensionality reduction prior to the clustering stage. By tailoring clustering methods to balance molecular and spatial information, it aims to reliably delineate microenvironments despite variations in signal dropout and resolution. The method is designed to overcome common technical biases and reinforces methodological plausibility by integrating advanced adaptive strategies as highlighted in the critiques.

proposals.title: Comprehensive Ligand–Receptor and Spatial Domain Integration
proposals.summary: This analysis bridges molecular signaling and spatial domain definition by comprehensively integrating ligand–receptor interaction data with neighborhood mapping. Using high-resolution spatial omics data, the method constructs detailed spatial graphs and applies clustering to identify domains with active intercellular communication. Differential expression and gene signature scoring are employed to validate the interaction-centric microdomains alongside traditional neighborhood compositions. This integrated approach successfully covers both cell–cell interaction and spatial heterogeneity themes, addressing critic concerns about overlapping analyses by clearly distinguishing its dual-focus strategy.

plan.user_request: Coordinate domain agents to propose, critique, and synthesize exactly 10 computational spatial-omics analyses likely performed in the hidden paper, producing draft, critique, and final JSON proposal files without executing the analyses.

steps.title: Draft candidate spatial-omics analyses
steps.description: Have the Spatial-CV Planning Agent (`spatial_cv_agent`) use only the PUBLIC BACKGROUND to generate exactly 10 distinct, computational spatial-omics analysis proposals focused on neighborhood-level spatial heterogeneity, microenvironments, and related geometry–composition questions, without executing any analysis. The agent must write these as a JSON file at `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` (e.g., a `proposals` list of items with `title` and brief `summary`), representing a first-pass hypothesis set of analyses likely used in the hidden paper.
steps.reasoning: A dedicated spatial-CV planner is best suited to translate the conceptual background into a coherent set of 10 plausible, diverse analysis ideas that emphasize neighborhood comparisons, recurrent microenvironments, differential regions, and interaction-oriented spatial statistics, while staying agnostic about the hidden paper’s specifics. Producing a concrete draft JSON artifact at the specified path establishes a fixed proposal set that downstream critique and synthesis steps can reference and improve.
steps.assignment_rationale: The spatial_cv_agent is explicitly designed to draft exactly 10 spatial-omics analysis proposals and to write hypotheses/draft_proposals.json, matching the required TA+CV treatment for step (1) and the spatial neighborhood focus of the task.

steps.title: Critique draft proposal set
steps.description: Have a Critic agent read `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and perform a structured critique of the 10 draft proposals, focusing on clarity, distinctness, coverage of key spatial-omics themes (neighborhood similarity, recurrent microenvironments, differential neighborhoods, ligand–receptor context, resolution/density effects), and methodological plausibility. The Critic must write its evaluation, including per-proposal comments and overarching suggestions for refinement and rebalancing, as a JSON critique report at `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json`.
steps.reasoning: A separate critique pass improves proposal quality by identifying redundancies, gaps (e.g., missing analyses on resolution effects or continuous transitions), and ambiguous or overly generic ideas before finalization. The dedicated critique artifact constrains and documents how the final synthesis should adjust the draft, enabling transparent, critique-informed refinement without directly altering the original proposals.
steps.assignment_rationale: The critic_agent is the dedicated review-only agent that produces hypotheses/critique.json, making it the correct choice to evaluate and comment on the draft proposals without altering them.

steps.title: Synthesize final proposal set
steps.description: Have a Hypothesis-style synthesis agent read both `project/outputs/hypotheses/draft_proposals.json` and `project/outputs/hypotheses/critique.json` and then construct the final set of exactly 10 computational spatial-omics analyses most consistent with the PUBLIC BACKGROUND and the Critic’s guidance. It must write `project/outputs/hypotheses/final_proposals.json` as a JSON object whose only top-level key is `proposals`, containing exactly 10 items, each an object with only `title` and a detailed `summary` that is self-contained, precise, and reflects the critique-informed refinement, without executing any of the proposed analyses.
steps.reasoning: A synthesis step is needed to reconcile the initial ideas with the critique, yielding a balanced, non-redundant, and well-articulated set of 10 proposals that collectively span key aspects of spatial neighborhood analysis (heterogeneity scores, recurrent microenvironments, condition differences, interaction contexts, and resolution/density controls). Writing the final proposals in the specified JSON schema produces the benchmark’s required deliverable, cleanly separated from the draft and critique artifacts.
steps.assignment_rationale: The hypothesis_agent is responsible for general-purpose hypothesis drafting and final synthesis, and it is the only agent advertised to write hypotheses/final_proposals.json, so it is best suited to integrate the critique and produce the final set of 10 proposals.

provenance.justification: Existing templates (e.g., paper_hypothesis_generation, hypothesis_testing) assume reading specific papers or running analyses and do not match this constrained three-step TA+CV workflow with fixed artifact paths and a required JSON proposal schema. The plan was therefore written from scratch to respect the benchmark’s exact step structure, agent roles (spatial_cv_agent, Critic, Hypothesis-style synthesis), and non-execution requirements.
